title: Calcium Imaging of Adult-Born Neurons in Freely Moving Mice
author: Carrier-Ruiz, Sugaya, et al.

steps.title: Prepare analysis workstation
steps.instruction: Ensure the computer meets the recommended specifications: ≥128 GB RAM, MATLAB 2020 or newer, Intel Core i7 processor (or newer), and a 1 TB SSD.

steps.title: Decompress raw video files
steps.instruction: Use the Inscopix image decompressor to convert raw video files to .hdf5 format, applying a down‑sampling factor of 4 during decompression to reduce disk usage and speed up loading.

substeps.instruction: Open the Inscopix image decompressor.
Select the raw video files to process.
Set the down‑sampling factor to 4.
Choose .hdf5 as the output format and start decompression.

steps.title: Preprocess video in Mosaic
steps.instruction: Import the .hdf5 video into Mosaic software and run the standard preprocessing workflow, selecting “fix defective pixels” and “fix isolated dropped frames.” Spatial down‑sampling is unnecessary if already performed during decompression.

substeps.instruction: Import the .hdf5 video file into Mosaic.
Open the preprocessing panel.
Check “fix defective pixels” and “fix isolated dropped frames.”
Run the preprocessing step.

steps.title: Motion‑correct video
steps.instruction: Perform motion correction in Mosaic (or compatible software) and save the corrected file as .h5. Choose a reference region containing many ABNs and clear spatial markers (e.g., blood vessels), set image contrast to 40 %–95 % of the maximum signal, and start with “translation only” correction; if residual motion remains, try rotation or expansion types and consider cropping unnecessary regions.

substeps.instruction: Save the preprocessed file in .h5 format.
Select a reference region with abundant ABNs and visible landmarks.
Adjust contrast to 40 %–95 % of the maximum observed signal.
Run motion correction using the “translation only” option.
If motion persists, repeat with rotation or expansion correction.
Optionally crop out regions that are not of interest to reduce false positives.

steps.title: Extract Ca2+ transients (CNMF‑E)
steps.instruction: In MATLAB, add the provided CNMF‑E script folder to the path, open ABNs_PV.m, set the video‑folder path on line 2 and the frame rate on line 46, then run the script. For short recordings, run demo_large_data_1p.m instead. For recordings longer than ~10 min (>30 000 frames), segment the video into overlapping batches of 1 000 frames using the multi‑batch implementation.

substeps.instruction: Create a folder containing the .h5 video files to be analyzed.
Add the CNMF‑E script folder (provided with the article) to the MATLAB path.
Open the file ABNs_PV.m.
Edit line 2 to input the full path to the video folder.
Edit line 46 to input the correct frame rate of the recordings.
Run ABNs_PV.m (or demo_large_data_1p.m for short videos).
If the recording exceeds ~10 min (>30 000 frames), split it into overlapping batches of 1 000 frames and run the multi‑batch CNMF‑E code.

steps.title: Quality‑control extracted components
steps.instruction: Visually inspect each extracted neuron, delete components that do not correspond to real neurons, and evaluate spatial and temporal quality using the provided MATLAB commands.

substeps.instruction: Run neuron.viewNeurons([], neuron.C_raw) to view raw traces and delete non‑neuronal components.
Run neuron.show_contours(0.6, [], neuron.PNR.*neuron.Cn, 1) to overlay contours on the PNR × CORR image; adjust PNR or CORR thresholds if contours are too few or too many.
Run implay(cat(2,mat2gray(neuron.PNR_all),mat2gray(neuron.Cn_all)),5) to browse PNR and CORR images in 1 000‑frame segments and look for motion artifacts.
Run stackedplot(neuron.C_raw) to display multiple Ca2+ traces simultaneously and identify overlapping square‑shaped transients that may indicate residual motion.
If many false positives are observed, repeat the CNMF‑E run with higher PNR or CORR thresholds.

steps.title: Track ABNs across sessions
steps.instruction: Motion‑correct each recording session independently in Mosaic, select a reference frame from one session, re‑motion‑correct the remaining sessions relative to that frame (or try alternative reference frames), then concatenate the sessions ensuring proper temporal alignment.

substeps.instruction: Open each session in Mosaic and perform motion correction as described in step 3.
Extract a single reference frame from one session (e.g., a frame with clear blood‑vessel landmarks).
For each of the other sessions, run motion correction using the extracted reference frame; if needed, test different reference frames for better alignment.
After all sessions are motion‑corrected, use Mosaic’s concatenation function to merge the sessions into a single file, verifying that the temporal order is correct.

steps.title: Analyze ABN activity and sleep
steps.instruction: After obtaining the raster plot of ABN activity, bin the data in 10‑second intervals and analyze sleep stages using Sleep Sign software (or alternative sleep‑analysis packages).

substeps.instruction: Export the ABN raster plot from MATLAB.
Load the raster data into Sleep Sign software.
Set bin size to 10 seconds and run the sleep‑stage analysis.
Optionally, use other sleep‑analysis tools such as the Sleep package (Combrisson et al., 2017) following their documentation.
